title: Sensitive-species generalization rule pack (geo/date coarsening) + conservation-expert sign-off
context: This is the project's highest-harm surface: publishing fine-grained sensitive-species coordinates can cause real-world poaching, collection, or disturbance harm. The rule pack resolves taxa against a sensitivity source and generalizes coordinates/dates/locality text, fail-closed. Per the plan this is treated as a high-stakes gate requiring credentialed conservation/data-steward expert sign-off before any partner relies on it; no sensitive-taxa dataset may be processed for reliance until that sign-off is recorded. Depends on csp-privacy-009.
objective: Author the sensitive-species generalization rule pack (coordinate-to-grid/centroid, date coarsening, exact-locality suppression) driven by a sensitivity source, fail-closed by default, and obtain and record credentialed conservation/data-steward expert sign-off before it is marked usable.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolves taxa against a sensitivity source (IUCN status / national / partner list, partner overrides) and generalizes coordinates to an agreed grid/centroid + coarsens dates + suppresses exact-locality text
Default fail-closed: unknown sensitivity yields generalization; generalization is never reversible from the output
Credentialed conservation/data-steward sign-off is recorded before the rule pack is marked usable; no sensitive-taxa dataset is processed for reliance until then
Rule pack is versioned and changelogged; any change re-triggers expert sign-off
output: rule-packs/sensitive-species-generalization/ containing the versioned generalization rule pack plus a recorded conservation/data-steward expert sign-off artifact.
